INT-001.title: Sahayogi Mail intake brief
INT-001.idea: Sahayogi Mail: a Sahayogi e-mail service for sending and receiving business mail with controlled delivery and privacy-conscious handling.
INT-001.problem_statement: Small and mid-size organisations rely on general e-mail products whose delivery problems, spam handling and administration are hard to see or control. When a message does not arrive, nobody can say whether it was never sent, deferred, bounced, filtered as spam or delivered.
INT-001.requested_solution: A Sahayogi-run mail service with a webmail interface, mailbox and domain administration, spam handling and a clear delivery status for every message.
INT-001.desired_outcome: Three pilot organisations send and receive their business mail on Sahayogi Mail, and every outbound message shows an accurate delivery status.
INT-001.purpose: Establish the verified AS-IS baseline of what already exists, then deliver a dependable mail service whose delivery, security and failures can be seen.

ADR-001.title: Separate the web application from the mail transport
ADR-001.context: Users need a clear delivery status and the transport must stay replaceable.
ADR-001.decision: The webmail application talks to the transport and mailbox storage only through the application API.
ADR-001.consequences: One more service to run; the status model lives in one place.
alternatives: Webmail directly on the mail server

ADR-002.title: Record delivery status from transport events
ADR-002.context: A message accepted by one component can fail later; users must not believe it was read or delivered when it was only accepted.
ADR-002.decision: Status is built from queue and delivery events and says "accepted by the receiving server", never "read".
ADR-002.consequences: Status can lag by seconds; the wording is stricter than a simple "sent".

ADR-003.title: Enforce TLS and domain authentication at the edge
ADR-003.context: Mail security depends on encrypted transport and on SPF, DKIM and DMARC being checked and signed.
ADR-003.decision: Require TLS where the other side supports it; sign outgoing mail with DKIM; check SPF, DKIM and DMARC on incoming mail.
ADR-003.consequences: Some old servers fall back to unencrypted delivery and are logged.

ADR-004.title: Keep message content out of logs
ADR-004.context: Logs are kept for operations and audit and must not expose message bodies or credentials.
ADR-004.decision: Log identifiers, sizes, status and timestamps only.
ADR-004.consequences: Debugging a content problem needs the user to resend a sample.

FSP-001.title: Specification: Mailbox and account management
FSP-001.preconditions: An administrator with a verified domain.
FSP-001.pre_checks: Domain verified, user limit not reached, name not in use.
FSP-001.main_flow: 1. Validate. 2. Create the mailbox. 3. Send the first-sign-in link. 4. Write the audit record.
FSP-001.state_data: Records move through the states in the Mail message life cycle.

FSP-001.testing_requirements: Happy path, invalid input, permission denied, upstream failure and retry.

FSP-002.title: Specification: Compose and send with delivery status
FSP-002.preconditions: The user is signed in and the mailbox is active.
FSP-002.pre_checks: Recipients are valid, size is within the limit, the user is not rate limited.
FSP-002.main_flow: 1. Validate. 2. Queue. 3. Hand to the transport. 4. Record each delivery event. 5. Show the status.
FSP-002.state_data: Records move through the states in the Mail message life cycle.
FSP-002.output: A status: queued, delayed, accepted by the receiving server, or failed with the reason.
FSP-002.edge_cases: Recipient rejected, server unreachable, retries exhausted, duplicate submit.
FSP-002.security_notes: Rate limit per mailbox; the body is never written to logs.
FSP-002.observability_notes: Log identifiers and outcome; alert on a rising failure rate.
FSP-002.testing_requirements: Happy path, invalid input, permission denied, upstream failure and retry.

FSP-003.title: Specification: Receive, filter and deliver incoming mail
FSP-003.preconditions: A hosted domain with an active mailbox.
FSP-003.trigger_input: A message arrives from an external server.
FSP-003.pre_checks: Recipient exists, size within limit, sender checks (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) evaluated.
FSP-003.main_flow: 1. Check the recipient. 2. Score the message. 3. Apply the policy. 4. Deliver, tag, quarantine or reject. 5. Log the decision.
FSP-003.state_data: Records move through the states in the Mail message life cycle.
FSP-003.output: The message in the inbox, the quarantine or rejected, with a logged reason.
FSP-003.edge_cases: Unknown mailbox, oversized message, policy engine unavailable, delivery to a full mailbox.
FSP-003.security_notes: Decisions are logged without message content.
FSP-003.observability_notes: Log identifiers and outcome; alert on a rising failure rate.
FSP-003.testing_requirements: Happy path, invalid input, permission denied, upstream failure and retry.

FSP-004.title: Specification: Spam quarantine and false-positive review
FSP-004.preconditions: A message held in quarantine by policy.
FSP-004.trigger_input: The user opens the quarantine list or reports a message.
FSP-004.main_flow: 1. List quarantined messages. 2. The user marks not spam or confirms. 3. Release or delete. 4. Count the false positive.
FSP-004.state_data: Records move through the states in the Mail message life cycle.
FSP-004.output: The message released to the inbox or removed, and a counted report.
FSP-004.edge_cases: Message released twice, mailbox full, report for a message already deleted.
FSP-004.security_notes: Only the mailbox owner and administrators can see quarantined mail.
FSP-004.observability_notes: Log identifiers and outcome; alert on a rising failure rate.
FSP-004.testing_requirements: Happy path, invalid input, permission denied, upstream failure and retry.

FSP-005.title: Specification: Domain authentication setup and check
FSP-005.preconditions: A domain added by an administrator.
FSP-005.trigger_input: The administrator runs the domain check.
FSP-005.pre_checks: The domain name is valid and owned by the organisation.
FSP-005.main_flow: 1. Show the records to publish. 2. Read DNS. 3. Compare. 4. Report each record as valid or missing.
FSP-005.state_data: Records move through the states in the Mail message life cycle.
FSP-005.output: A per-record result and signing enabled for verified domains.
FSP-005.edge_cases: DNS temporarily unavailable, record published with a typo, propagation delay.
FSP-005.security_notes: Private keys never leave the signing service.
FSP-005.observability_notes: Log identifiers and outcome; alert on a rising failure rate.
FSP-005.testing_requirements: Happy path, invalid input, permission denied, upstream failure and retry.

FSP-006.title: Specification: Administrator message trace and audit trail
FSP-006.trigger_input: The administrator searches for a message.
FSP-006.pre_checks: The administrator role is present for this organisation.
FSP-006.main_flow: 1. Search by sender, recipient and time. 2. Show the message path. 3. Write an audit record of the search.
FSP-006.state_data: Records move through the states in the Mail message life cycle.
FSP-006.output: The message path with each step and an audit entry.

FSP-006.security_notes: Users without the role are refused; the audit trail cannot be edited.
FSP-006.observability_notes: Log identifiers and outcome; alert on a rising failure rate.
FSP-006.testing_requirements: Happy path, invalid input, permission denied, upstream failure and retry.
